children: Retail and food services sales totalled $774bn last month, up 1.2% from July when sales fell 0.5%, government data showed.
This was 6.0% higher than August 2025 and the strongest growth rate seen since March, coming in comfortably ahead of the 0.8% increase expected by analysts.
Excluding motor vehicles and parts, sales increased 1.4% on the month, while sales excluding both autos and petrol stations rose 1.2%.

Among the major categories, petrol-station sales jumped 3.1%, while non-store retailers, which include online sellers, saw sales rise 2.6%. Electronics and appliance stores recorded a 1.6% increase, while spending at food services and drinking places was up 1.2%.
Motor vehicle and parts dealers saw sales increase 0.6%, while clothing-store sales rose 0.7%.
Building-material and garden-equipment sales edged down 0.2%, while department-store sales fell 0.8%.
